transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. It's, um, very nice to meet you. Thank you for seeing me, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, I'm... I guess I'm here because of some things going on at work. I do environmental modeling—mathematical sciences—and... well, I really don't want to sound like a difficult person, or like I'm pointing fingers, but I'm pretty sure the people on our current contract have been tracking my revisions. And, um, planting errors in the datasets. I think they're trying to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

My wife, and even the junior analysts at the office, they keep telling me it's just, you know, normal version-control mistakes. And I try to listen to them, I really do. But... I don't know, does that make sense? I just wanted to get a professional opinion to make sure I'm handling this the right way. Is it okay that we start with that?
How long have you been noticing and worrying about this pattern of your coworkers altering your data—days, weeks, or longer?

Well, um, I don't want to make it sound like I'm obsessing over it, or... or being a bad team player. I always try to be really easy to work with. But, um... as far as being, well, certain that they're tracking the revisions and... and planting those errors? I'd say it's been about the last two months. Give or take. 

I kept it to myself at first because I really didn't want to point fingers unfairly, you know? But the pattern just kept showing up in the datasets. So it's been about two months of being sure about it. I really hope I don't sound, I don't know, overly suspicious saying that out loud. Does that timeline make sense for what you're asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Besides these suspicions about your data being altered, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that others couldn't perceive?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I, uh, I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I was... well, that things were that severe. I've never heard any voices or seen anything that wasn't really there. 

I know my concerns about the contract team might sound a little... intense, maybe? But I promise I'm completely grounded in reality. It's really just the numbers and the datasets I'm looking at, nothing outside of that. 

I hope it's a good thing that I don't have anything like that to report? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, and I'd really hate for you to think I'm... well, losing my mind or being unreasonable. Am I answering your question the right way?

Aside from this situation at work, have you generally, throughout your life, found it hard to trust other people—like friends, family, or past coworkers—suspecting they might be exploiting or deceiving you, even without solid evidence?

Oh, gosh, no. No, not at all. I really hope I haven't come across as... well, as a cynical person, or someone who is always looking for a fight. I've always prided myself on being a very trusting person. 

My wife and I have a wonderful relationship, and I've always gotten along great with my friends and past coworkers. I usually take people at their word, and I really try my best to be a good, easygoing guy to be around. That's actually why this whole thing with the current contract is so... upsetting to me, I guess. It's completely out of the ordinary for me to feel this way about people I work with. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just naturally suspicious of everyone. I always try to see the best in people. Does that help answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context so I don't give you the wrong impression of my character.

Aside from this situation with your coworkers and the data, have you noticed any other unusual beliefs or suspicions in different areas of your life—like about neighbors, strangers, or things you see in the news—that seem connected or similar in nature?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. Um... I really hope I haven't painted myself as some sort of... well, conspiracy theorist or someone who's paranoid about the world. I promise I'm not like that at all. 

My neighbors are wonderful people, and I don't really watch the news looking for, um, hidden meanings or anything like that. It's really just... well, strictly the anomalies in the datasets at work. That's the absolute only thing. Outside of that, I just live a quiet life. I try to be a good neighbor and a friendly person to strangers. 

I really want to make sure I'm being helpful to you here—does that answer what you were asking? I just don't want you to think I have a habit of being suspicious of everyone, because I really do try to be as agreeable as possible.
